speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister Lawrence Wong and I first spoke about COVID-19 in Parliament in January.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And I updated Members again during the COS debate earlier this month.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As the task force involves multiple Ministries, may I have your permission, Mr Speaker, to invite the relevant Ministers to respond to clarifications on their respective responsibilities?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As of yesterday, there are more than 370,000 COVID-19 cases and over 16,500 fatalities from the disease worldwide, and the epicentre has shifted to Europe and, perhaps, United States.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The number of deaths in Italy alone has exceeded that in China.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: World Health Organization (WHO) declared COVID-19 a pandemic on 11 March.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: How the outbreak develops globally will depend on the strategies and efforts of countries around the world.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: WHO has advised that we can still change the course of the pandemic if all countries take the necessary actions to contain the outbreak.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Otherwise, we will continue to see the number of affected countries and cases rise rapidly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Regions such as China, Hong Kong and Taiwan, had experienced a reduction in the number of cases a few weeks ago, but have started to see increases in new cases in the past few days driven by imported cases, arising mainly from residents returning from abroad.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: From late-January to February, Singapore saw an initial wave of imported cases from China.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Some of these resulted in several local transmission chains, such as the Life Church and Missions and Grace Assembly of God combined cluster which resulted in 31 cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: However, in recent weeks, we are seeing a second wave of imported cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The top three sources of importation to Singapore are the United Kingdom, the United States and Indonesia.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And over the coming weeks, the number of cases will continue to rise, as some of our around 200,000 overseas Singaporeans return home from all over the world.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have slowed the local spread thus far through a three-pronged approach: first, reducing importation; second, detecting and isolating cases early; and third, emphasising social responsibility and good personal hygiene habits.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: To reduce the risk of importation, we have stemmed the inflow of travellers by imposing border controls and issued travel advisories to advise Singaporeans to defer their travel plans until the situation around the world is under control.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Minister Lawrence Wong will elaborate on this later in his speech.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have also strengthened checks at our borders to detect and isolate cases before they come into contact with the Singapore community.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For example, since January, we have progressively put in place temperature screening, health checks and swabbing at all our checkpoints.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: All who meet the suspect case definition are conveyed directly to the hospital, while all symptomatic travellers as well as some selected travellers are swabbed as a precautionary measure.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Beyond our checkpoints, we have also put in place a system to detect cases early, through surveillance at hospitals, polyclinics as well as Public Health Preparedness Clinics.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have re-activated Public Health Preparedness Clinics just over a month ago and today, we have more than 900 clinics offering subsidised consultation and treatment for Singaporeans and Permanent Residents with respiratory illnesses.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Singapore residents have benefited from more than 267,000 subsidised attendances at these clinics thus far, on top of that at our polyclinics.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These tests are important in helping us to detect as many cases as possible and as early as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The moment a case is confirmed, we activate contact tracing to identify close contacts and quarantine them as soon as possible, so as to reduce further spread of the disease.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Government has put in place many measures to reduce imported cases, and to trace and isolate any such cases as soon as possible to prevent spread.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But every one of us needs to play our part in practising good personal hygiene, social responsibility and safe distancing to further reduce the risk of local transmission.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Minister Lawrence Wong will elaborate on these later.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I hope that Singaporeans will support these measures and keep up good hygiene habits which will play an increasingly important role in our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: During the COS debate, I mentioned Singapore's efforts in developing research and knowledge on COVID-19 and sharing these with other countries.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There is an article today in today's paper about an innovative rapid test kit being developed by A*STAR's researchers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We hope they will go to trial soon and give us an additional weaponry against COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For treatment, a COVID-19 therapeutic workgroup comprising members from various hospitals across different disciplines as well as Health Sciences Authority or HSA, has been set up to work on guidelines for repurposed drugs with antiviral activity, such as Lopinavir-ritonavir, Interferon Beta-1B and hydroxychloroquine, to treat infected patients in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The National Centre for Infectious Diseases or NCID, and Tan Tock Seng Hospital, together with Singapore Blood Blank, have initiated donor recruitment to collect convalescent blood plasma from recovered patients to treat other COVID-19 patients.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Our doctors have also been participating in international clinical trials, with collaborators such as the US National Institutes of Health.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For vaccines, scientists all over the world have successfully isolated and cultured the virus, which will aid the development of a vaccine.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The international community is also working together to identify vaccine candidates and conduct clinical trials.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For example, some institutes such as Moderna Inc have already started human trials as of last week.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We do not know how long the pandemic will last, but we have to plan on the basis that COVID-19 will be with us for a long while, maybe till the end of the year or longer and ensure that we have the resources and capabilities to see us through.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: COVID-19 has also taken a toll on our economy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The impact will extend way beyond the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Many Singaporeans and businesses will need to make adjustments as this is not something that will be over quickly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The measures we announced yesterday will impact many businesses and workers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Government will introduce greater support for the economy and our workers in response to this situation.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Members of Parliament have asked about healthcare capacity.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will ensure that we have sufficient capacity to meet our healthcare needs not only for COVID-19 patients but also for other patients.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We had invested significantly in the past to ensure that we have sufficient healthcare capacity to manage infectious outbreaks.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: To preserve capacity and resources for those who most need it, clinicians at our public hospitals had earlier reviewed their patients and deferred non-urgent appointments and elective procedures where clinically appropriate to do so.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They have continued to see patients with higher needs to ensure that they receive timely care.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When appointments had to be deferred, the public hospitals have worked to ensure that patients received sufficient supportive care.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are also exploring collaborations with private hospitals for some non-COVID-19 patients to be cared for there instead.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We already have on-going collaborations with some of them and some of these can be stepped up so that we can preserve capacity in our public hospitals to manage the outbreak.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Patients transferred to these private hospitals through such collaborations will continue to pay similar rates they would have paid at our public hospitals.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The most important resource, actually, is our healthcare staff.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They have been working tirelessly to make sure that our patients, COVID-19 or otherwise, are well taken care of.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I want to take this opportunity to thank our healthcare workers once again for their dedication.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We recognise the heavy workload and stress that our healthcare workers face every day.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The surge in patient load due to COVID-19 means that some are taking on longer shifts, while others are required to take on additional roles.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: To ensure the well-being of our healthcare workers, institutions will make sure that their staff are well-rested and have put in place a series of measures to reduce staff burnout, such as counselling services and peer support programmes.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Most importantly, every case we can avoid will help to lighten their load.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Hence, each of us can help by doing the right thing to reduce the risk of transmission.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I also want to also thank Singaporeans for your resilience, your understanding and support in adapting to these new measures and changes quickly and putting up with inconveniences and disruptions to your daily lives for the sake of other Singaporeans and our community.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: With the global situation still evolving and the number of cases rising rapidly worldwide, we must prepare to see more cases here too in time to come.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Yesterday, we had 17 local cases in addition to 32 imported ones.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We must work together and do what we can to keep the number of local cases down.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: With a significant number of imported cases from returning residents and visitors, we have progressively put in place travel restrictions and placed returning residents on the Stay-Home Notice (SHN) and quarantine, but there is still a risk of them leading to more localised transmissions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As more clusters emerge, our contact tracing, quarantine and healthcare resources will be stretched.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If the clusters grow too large, such as those we see in the Life Church and Missions and Grace Assembly of God or SAFRA Jurong, if we have a few of them at the same time, it will be very difficult to contain them effectively, and the pressure on our healthcare system will increase.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: While we still have sufficient capacity in our healthcare system today, we cannot be complacent and we will need to preserve our buffer capacity.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Previously, all confirmed COVID-19 cases, regardless of severity, were admitted to our hospitals and remained there until they were tested negative for the virus twice, over a period of 24 hours, and this takes up our capacity.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That means many of the COVID-19 cases in our hospitals experience mild symptoms, no more than that of flu.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Patients at these facilities will continue to be quarantined and closely monitored, so there is no risk to the general public in the community.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Similar to cases admitted to hospitals, patients will be closely monitored and repeatedly tested for the virus.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At this point, they will no longer have any risk of transmitting the virus to others as they have fully recovered.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will continue to explore the use of such isolation facilities for our well and stable COVID-19 patients.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This way, we can focus our critical hospital resources on the seriously ill, to minimise the number of fatalities.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But rest assured that any Singaporean who requires medical care, whether for COVID-19 or other illnesses, will receive the necessary treatment and care.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: While we implement plans to ensure sufficient healthcare capacity, it is equally important to prevent new local clusters in the first place.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This way, we can try to avoid an exponential growth in the number of infections, which could quickly overwhelm the healthcare system, as we saw in Hubei and Italy; and increasingly so, in many other countries.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Singapore's strategy is to slow down the infection rate and maintain it at as low a level for as long as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: A lower infection rate will help us to better conduct epidemiological investigations, contact tracing and quarantining of close contacts, so as to prevent further spread of the disease in the community.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It also preserves healthcare capacity to care for the more severe cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If we do nothing, the number of cases will shoot up, like what happened in several cities and countries recently.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Then, our only hope is that most of the population get infected and become immune quickly, and the rate of infection will start to slow down as more become immune, or a vaccine or a cure is found.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is when the curve starts to trend downwards.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This scenario is very attractive, we get over with it very quickly, but there are unfortunately, two major risks.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: First, an uncontrolled spike in the number of cases in a short period of time, like the purple curve, will overwhelm the healthcare system, easily resulting in high mortality rates, and there is no turning back once you are on this track.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The second risk is that it is not certain yet that this immunity will be effective or sustained.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, one alternative, is to introduce stringent safe distancing and other measures to slow down the infection curve, to slow down the infection rate.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The number will still grow but if we do it right, we will end up with a lower peak.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is commonly known as flattening the curve, as Members can see, on the blue curve.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But by flattening the curve, we may actually stretch out the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, Members see a long tail, meaning it will take much longer for the pandemic to be over.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, for Singapore, today, we are still at the start of the curve, so we have a chance, we have a chance to do neither.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We hope, that if we do it right, we can significantly slow down the growth as much as we can, until the whole pandemic is over, without either a sharp peak or a long tail.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This may sound impossible, because this are the two curves that have been established by academics.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But, impossible as it may sound, we have to try our best to do so.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: To achieve this, we have to continue to strengthen our efforts to detect cases early to initiate the contact tracing process as soon as possible to reduce the risk of the infection spreading.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are also leveraging technology to supplement our contact tracing efforts.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This will be useful if you have come into close contact with a confirmed case which you do not know.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: By downloading and activating this app, the contact tracers will be able to inform you early so that you can isolate yourself and protect your family, or receive early treatment if you are already unwell.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For those who are concerned about privacy, I would like to assure you that the app does not track your location, so where you go, does not matter, the app does not know.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It uses Bluetooth to detect if you have been in close proximity for more than 30 minutes with someone else with the app switched on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I urge Members and all Singaporeans to download the app to protect yourselves and your families.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I have spoken multiple times about the importance of social responsibility, here in Parliament as well as publicly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Government will continue to put in place measures to protect Singaporeans as I have shared earlier, but the daily actions of each one of us will go a long way in winning this war.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If you have been issued with a quarantine order or Stay-Home Notice, please stay at home and abide by the requirements of the order or notice.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If you violate them, there will be penalties and the heaviest penalty is that you may infect others, including those you love.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If you are unwell, please wear a mask and see a doctor immediately.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If you have been given a medical certificate, please stay home for the whole duration covered by the medical certificate.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Wash your hands with soap regularly and do not touch your face.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is literally in our hands to contain this outbreak.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In Singapore, we saw a few local clusters emerge where individuals who were feeling unwell or were issued a Medical Certificate but did not minimise social contact and continued to attend work or social activities.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have encouraged employers to support employees to spend the necessary time away from the office so that they can recover.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is not just about ourselves, but those around us too, including our loved ones.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For the young and healthy among us, we may get away with a mild cold or cough, but for the more vulnerable loved ones around us, the disease may prove to be more serious.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we must not take social responsibility lightly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have been progressively putting in place safe distancing measures, especially for the vulnerable groups.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For example, after the SAFRA Jurong cluster arose, we suspended all senior-activities at Community Centres, Residents Committees, Senior Activity Centres and others.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: While some Members of Parliament, I think, Ms Denise Phua, asked me at the last Sitting whether we can resume some of these activities, I was very happy to say yes, then.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Now, I am afraid it will be a while longer before we do that, to protect the seniors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For example, they can exercise at home with TV and online exercise programmes, as well as enjoy broadcast programmes covering singing, so they do not need to join karaoke groups, but they can join TV programmes and sing-along; cooking and other programmes by celebrities and People's Association trainers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Family members and care-givers of seniors should also take precautions such as washing hands with soap and water before interacting with seniors and refraining from visiting seniors if one is unwell.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Each of us needs to play our part to take care of our seniors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: With these added precautions in place, seniors can continue staying active and healthy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: While we should keep a wider physical distance between ourselves and others, we need to close the emotional distance between us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As Prime Minister pointed out, this is as much a psychological battle as it is a medical one.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: To win the battle, we must close ranks while keeping a safe physical distance.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We should not stop caring about fellow Singaporeans or build walls between ourselves.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On the contrary, we need to be more united than ever so that we can ride through this crisis together.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We can show our appreciation to our frontline workers who are working very hard to keep Singapore clean and Singaporeans safe, and show our support to colleagues and friends who have acted responsibly and isolated themselves when they feel unwell.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Minister for National Development will be making a related Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will allow Members raise points of clarifications on both statements after this statement.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Minister Gan mentioned just now, we experienced an initial wave of imported cases from China, which resulted in some local transmission and local clusters.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now, we are facing a second and much bigger wave of imported cases from the rest of the world, especially from America and Europe.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It reflects how quickly virus is spreading around the world outside of China.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The number of cases is doubling every four to six days.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are more cases outside China than in China now.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are not alone in facing this new wave of imported cases.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many places in Asia – Hong Kong, Taiwan are in a similar situation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we have been rapidly adjusting and updating our measures to respond to this new challenge.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have progressively tightened our border controls and travel restrictions, based on the rapidly changing situation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We started with restrictions, as Members would recall, for travellers from China; we extended the restrictions to other epidemic centres – initially to Republic of Korea, Italy, Iran, then France, Germany, Spain; and later UK, Switzerland, Japan and the ASEAN countries.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Eventually, we did not have to do country by country, we covered the whole world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are very significant moves for a small open economy like Singapore, where we have always been connected to the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But these are extraordinary times, this is an unprecedented crisis and we had to move decisively to keep our borders safe.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Importantly, we want to focus our resources on the large number of returning Singaporeans coming back from overseas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We identify those coming back with symptoms as early as possible, right at the airport.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are testing as many as possible and we are expanding our testing capacity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also know that we cannot rely on tests alone, because someone who tests negative at the point of entry may simply be incubating the virus and could develop symptoms over the following days.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why it is important to also isolate these returnees and have all of them have to serve a 14-day Stay-Home Notice.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the numbers will rise with the growing number of returnees.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many are understandably concerned about the risk of the Stay-Home Notice returnees infecting their family members.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These returnees have to stay in their rooms throughout.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They cannot use any of the hotel facilities, swimming pool or gym; fourteen days in the room and we will put in place tight security arrangements to ensure this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For those who have already returned and are presently still serving the Stay-Home Notices at home, they, too, can apply to stay in these designated hotels if they so prefer.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is a huge operational and logistical undertaking, given the volumes of people we are receiving everyday.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are able to make use of the empty bed spaces in hotels but we still need to ramp up manpower to enforce their self-isolation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I want to acknowledge the hard work of all our public officials who did an excellent job in getting this ready within a very short period of time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is no telling how long this current wave of returnees and imported cases will last.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With more lockdowns imposed in countries elsewhere, more may want to return here to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we have to be prepared for more returnees and have arrangements to ensure that they are self-isolated for the full period before they can be brought back within our community.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we do not want Singaporeans to travel overseas at this time and to compound the problem.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we have raised our travel advisory to the highest level to defer all travel.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I think people regard many things as essential.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those who choose to do so will have to pay full costs should they need treatment for COVID-19 when they return.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, they will be subject to a full 14-day self-isolation at the hotel which they will also have to pay in full.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite our best efforts at controlling these flows at the borders, we have to be prepared for more cases to emerge, especially given the large number of returnees.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why it is critical to quickly identify and isolate these cases and their close contacts through our on-going efforts at contact tracing and quarantine.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Minister Gan spoke about this and how we are going to ramp up our capacity to do more contact tracing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is essential because the minute you give up on contact tracing, then you are no longer able to manage the virus outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is the situation that many countries are facing now – they are no longer able to contact-trace the cases as well as their close contacts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we want to continue to maintain contact tracing and put all the close contacts under quarantine.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As of last night, there are around 2,500 persons under quarantine, be it in their homes or in Government Quarantine Facilities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue with the tough enforcement for both Stay-Home Notice and quarantine cases, including through all the various means we have put in place –remote monitoring, video calls and random house visits.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But as Minister Gan said just now, the biggest penalty is not just a fine or even a jail sentence but the costs that you impose on others if you were to breach these rules.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have an excellent detection system to pick up COVID-19 cases through our contact tracing procedures.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One Harvard study called our contact tracing system the "gold standard".

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But even then, our detection rate is not 100%.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That means that the virus continues to circulate in our population and there are still cases out there in the community which will pop up.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We monitor very closely the number of locally-transmitted cases, especially the ones that are unlinked – "unlinked" meaning that they are new, they are popping up and we do not know where they originate from.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are seeing more of such cases in recent days.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we need to put in place a whole range of additional public health measures to slow down the spread of the virus within Singapore itself.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We can think of these additional public health measures at different levels.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, we have baseline measures which we are already doing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Things like daily temperature taking, seeing a doctor if you are unwell and staying at home and not shaking hands.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now, in true multiracial Singapore style, we have different ways of doing it.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You can do the “Salam Mufti”, traditional Chinese style or Namaste.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I think all of us are practising this in our daily lives now.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We uphold good personal hygiene; wash our hands regularly and do not use our hands to touch our face and we uphold better public hygiene standards.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are stepping this up through SG Clean, a whole-of-nation effort that Minister Masagos is overseeing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of these measures should be continued for a sustained period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, some ought to be new permanent norms, like upholding higher hygiene standards and using common serving utensils instead of double dipping.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, even after the COVID-19 outbreak is over – and it will be over after a while – we should continue to practise some of these new norms as a permanent part of our lives.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am not sure about the not-shaking-hands part.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Frankly, at some point in time, we might want to get back to having some physical contact, but certainly not now.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, many things we will do on a sustained basis, some on a permanent basis even.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But beyond the baseline measures, we need to rely on additional measures and that is what we call social or safe distancing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We can think of these measures as extra "brakes" that we apply to slow down the spread of the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last Friday, we introduced a first set of safe distancing measures.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We suspended senior group activities; we pushed for telecommuting and staggered hours at workplaces; we limited large events to less than 250 persons, and we said seats have to be apart, like what we are doing now in Parliament; and we wanted a 1-metre spacing in public spaces and F&B outlets.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, public sector agencies are now pushing very hard on telecommuting.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Where it is not possible, for example, for frontline and operational units, the agencies have implemented split teams by location or shifts, as well as staggered work hours, wherever it is practical.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the efforts on telecommuting must go beyond the public sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All workplaces must go on telecommuting as default wherever they can.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More employers are doing this, but some are still resistant and want their staff to be physically present in their offices when they can actually work from home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will get all employers to push more aggressively on telecommuting.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is the only way to allow Singaporeans to continue working while minimising their movements and contacts outside and it is also how we can reduce the load on our public transport system, especially during peak hours.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The measures introduced last week have brought about changes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When you go out, you can see that perceptibly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We now see alternate seats marked in dining venues, including in hawker centres and coffee shops.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we have to move faster, much faster.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We still hear anecdotes of people going to discos and night clubs, and gathering in large groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In schools and workplaces, we have been taking precautions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For schools, for example, Minister Ong Ye Kung and the MOE team have put in place a range of measures to keep students safe.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we do not allow intermingling of students outside of the classroom.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In workplaces, too, we are getting employers to take precautions, getting their staff to be seated separately and, as I have mentioned earlier, pushing harder on telecommuting.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With this significant slowing down of activities and movements, we hope we can break the potential transmission chains that may be happening.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are very major moves to slow down the spread of the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise the inconvenience and disruption that these measures will bring to people’s lives and to businesses, but we have no easy options.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is the reality that countries everywhere are facing in tackling the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The more we try to stop or slow down the virus, the steeper will be the damage on our economies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we have to do what is necessary from the public health point of view first to save lives, slow down the virus and then, thereafter, do our best to manage the economic consequences.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the last few days, even as the Task force was deliberating over these measures, we have been sharing them, updating the MOF and economic teams working on the package of measures which Deputy Prime Minister Heng will be announcing tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I urge all Singaporeans to cooperate and take the latest set of measures very seriously.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our main message to everyone is this: minimise your non-essential activities and your contact with others during this period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You can talk about all the suspensions, different settings, but simple message – everyone minimise your non-essential activities and your contact with others during this period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must all do our part to stop the spread of the disease and ensure that we do not end up with a major outbreak of new local clusters.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The latest measures may help to slow down the spread of the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it is also possible that despite these measures, the number of infected cases will continue to rise.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will keep the measures under constant review.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If the situation worsens, we will apply extra brakes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If the situation improves, we may be able to ease off a little bit but not go back to baseline; perhaps to a less stringent set of measures because the pandemic will probably still not be over for quite some time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Given that we have been tightening our measures recently, I can understand why Singaporeans may also be concerned about the availability of essential supplies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, we have been planning for potential disruption of supplies, be it food or medical supplies, over many years through stockpiling, local production and diversification of our overseas sources.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Minister Chan Chun Sing and the MTI team are overseeing this work and they have been steadily ramping up their efforts across all fronts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If many people start to build up their own individual stockpiles at home unnecessarily, it will lead to an apparent shortage on the supermarket shelves and deprive others who may have more urgent need for food and other essential supplies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Such a perception could precipitate more panic buying, which can quickly spiral out of control.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There was, indeed, some concern initially when Malaysia imposed a Movement Control Order earlier this month.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The flow of goods and cargo, including food supplies, are largely continuing although we still have to be prepared there may well be disruptions along the way.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As far as people movement is concerned, we have quickly found accommodations for the Malaysian workers who decided to stay in Singapore and this has allowed essential services like public transport to continue without interruption.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Going forward, the Singapore-Malaysia Special Working Committee, co-chaired by Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean and Senior Minister Dato Sri' Ismail Sabri on the Malaysian side, is discussing a joint mitigation plan to ensure the safe and sustainable movement of people, goods and essential services between our two countries.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, if you have been following the news, Malaysia has now just extend its movement restrictions to 14 April, a few more weeks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If and when the Movement Control Order in Malaysia is lifted, we cannot go back to business as usual and have large groups of people moving across our land checkpoints on a daily basis.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That will be too dangerous from a public health point of view.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will need extra precautions on both sides, which are being worked out, so as to minimise the spread of the virus across our land borders.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Underpinning all of these efforts is the need for all Singaporeans to take individual and social responsibility.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The fight against the virus cannot be done by frontline workers or Government agencies alone.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Each and every one of us has to actively do our part.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And there are many things that we all can do, which Minister Gan mentioned earlier: upholding good personal hygiene; taking of temperature daily; seeing a doctor if you are unwell; staying at home if that is the case; and if you have just returned from overseas, ensure you self-isolate for 14 days, even from your family members; and minimising of non-essential activities and contact with others during this period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are all enlisted in this national effort to slow down the spread of the virus and if we are disciplined about this, we will have a chance to control the situation and to protect ourselves, our family members, and the people around us.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In these difficult times, we see the best of Singapore and Singaporeans at work.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had young people from the Youth Corps conducting door-to-door visits to share personal hygiene and safety tips with the elderly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have had many volunteer groups like the Singapore Red Cross stepping up their befriending calls to many isolated seniors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had many individuals and volunteers also packing and donating care packs and items like masks, hand sanitisers and thermometers to the elderly and vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In these difficult times, we see Singaporeans from all walks of life working flat out to fight the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have healthcare workers on the frontline making many sacrifices and working tirelessly to care for patients.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have our public officials working very hard, too, across all the agencies – not everything they do is visible to the public eye.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I can tell you that they are working round the clock and it is incredible what they have been able to achieve, especially given the quick turnaround times.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are literally making new measures every other day, putting in place adjustments to measures almost on a daily basis and so this impacts on communications.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have a huge team working night and day to put out public communications materials to inform the public of all of these updates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have a huge team on the operational side, be it at immigration or security, going all out to adjust to these changes and ensuring smooth implementation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From time to time, there will be public feedback, there will be public complaints – they take all of this in their stride.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If there are lapses, they try to rectify them as quickly as possible.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I hope the public will cooperate, too.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We welcome feedback but you can do your part by ensuring the accuracy of your feedback so that the agencies do not have to waste time and resources to check on each and every information.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are many more unsung heroes all over the island – in areas like cleaning, security, airport management, media, hotels, F&B, transport and many more providing services to Singaporeans – all still going strong, keeping their spirits high.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And there are many Singaporeans who have stepped up in their own ways looking after one another and caring for our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Words are not sufficient to express our appreciation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Words are not sufficient to express our appreciation for so many Singaporeans going all out to fight the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I just want to say a big "thank you" to everyone who is doing their part.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise that there is a growing uncertainty, anxiety and fear amongst Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: People are asking many questions – how long will this last?

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I receive many suggestions and feedback all the time, every day.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some say we are doing too much and there are too many restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I cannot reply to each one of them, individually, but the team is looking at all of them and we take all of them into consideration as we develop and update our measures.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In some cases, there are no clear answers and solutions because the situation is so uncertain – so fluid and changing rapidly by the day.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But one thing is clear – we are all in this together and we will continue to work through the challenges together, every step of the way.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It looks to be obvious – the COVID-19 outbreak will be long drawn.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Then, Dr Tan says, call fresh elections when COVID is no longer a crisis.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Perhaps, I can invite Senior Minister Teo to speak on this topic.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: It is a global pandemic and an unprecedented global crisis.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In Europe and the US, the virus is still spreading at an exponential rate.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Financial markets are in their worst turmoil since 2008.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Hence, on 14 March, Prime Minister Lee warned that we face a grave and extended challenge.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The pandemic “is likely to last at least this year, and quite possibly longer”.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Even after we deal with this pandemic, the economic repercussion will last longer, with significant and longstanding impact on both lives and livelihoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In Singapore, the Government took early and decisive action to protect our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We have managed the COVID-19 situation for now, with tremendous effort and cooperation from everyone.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: But the situation remains very serious and continues to develop quickly.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We are starting to see another wave of imported cases – mainly from returning Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Multi-Ministry Task Force has introduced measures to deal with this.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: But the situation may get worse, before it eventually gets better.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Our focus now, of this Government, is on being prepared for the long haul, through the end of this year and beyond, and focus on solving this problem with Singaporeans and for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Ideally, we would like to conduct elections in normal conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The present situation is not ideal for holding an election, but that does not mean it makes an election impossible.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: As the Prime Minister said, no decision has been taken yet on the timing of a GE.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In making such a decision, the overriding concern is what is best for Singapore and for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Some have suggested only holding elections when we see the "tail-end of the virus spread".

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: And this is, indeed, the dilemma that we face.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Prime Minister has laid out the choices clearly.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The longer we wait, the more unpredictable, difficult and dangerous it could be.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Compounding this will be the uncertainty that comes with when the election will be held as we go through the year, trying to face this crisis together.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Alternatively, the country can go for early elections, settle who will lead the country through this major crisis, and give the Government a clear and fresh mandate, a full term ahead and legitimacy to take major decisions, tough decisions in the interest of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Today, more than ever, we need a government that the people has expressed confidence in, to take us through this unprecedented health crisis, stabilise the economy and safeguard our people's lives and livelihood.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: You want to make sure that he is there together with you, working with you, guiding you through the storm.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: It is not a good idea to place all our hopes in the situation improving before April 2021, and add the uncertainty of when an election will be held to the uncertainties that are already ahead of us.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: However, we should not close off any options.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We have been upfront and open with Singaporeans about the challenges we face, the dilemmas, considerations and different possibilities so that Singaporeans will understand why there might be a need to go ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: However, some suggestions about this issue have been misleading and unhelpful.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: For example, the suggestion to delay the elections beyond the required time-frame of April 2021 until the crisis is over and to have the President form a caretaker government consisting of some of the current Members of Parliament.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Singapore is one of the only newly independent Commonwealth countries to regularly hold elections and has never declared a state of emergency since 1965.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Declaring an emergency and putting off elections indefinitely is not a precedent we should set lightly.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: A President's power to declare an emergency can only be exercised on the advice of the Cabinet.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Even if the President proclaims an emergency, given that the incumbent Cabinet remains in office during an emergency, there is no legal basis or practical need for the President to form a new government.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Even if there is a caretaker government under a state of emergency, it would by definition be a caretaker.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: It would be hobbled by the fact that it lacks the explicit mandate of voters and would therefore not be in a position to take major decisions on behalf of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This is the reason why constitutional convention requires that a caretaker government not make any far-reaching or long-term measure.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Just when we need a government with a clear mandate to pull out all the stops in a crisis to implement strong mitigation measures, to mobilise our resources and reserves to implement strong economic stabilisation measures to save jobs and livelihoods, and to steer the country through the COVID-19 crisis, a caretaker government would not have a mandate to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: How can this be in the best interests of the country and our people?

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Putting forward constitutionally unworkable proposals at a time of serious national crisis can only confuse and mislead Singaporeans, to the detriment of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This discussion on the impact of COVID-19 on our elections is an important one.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This Government is ever mindful that what is at stake are jobs, businesses and lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Our decision must be based on what is in the best interests of Singapore and Singaporeans, and how we can move forward together.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: On Mr Christopher de Souza's second question – he asked about holding elections safely amidst the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The safety of all Singaporeans is of utmost importance.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: To combat the virus spread, we have implemented comprehensive measures over the past few weeks at every level.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We have heard Minister Gan and Minister Wong – travel restrictions, quarantines, social distancing measures, strengthening our healthcare institutions, workplace measures, protecting our students in schools and supply of essential goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: All these necessary measures will still be maintained.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: This means that the necessary extra safeguards and precautions must and will be taken, whether the elections are held early or held later, at every step – nominations, campaigning and voting.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We will have to make all the necessary arrangements to ensure that parties can campaign effectively and people can vote safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: For example, for campaigning, we can have live-streaming of speeches on the Internet and adequate television time for candidates.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: For voting, we already have special express lanes for seniors and those who need them.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We can also have social distancing while queuing, proper hand hygiene for voting paraphernalia and hand sanitisers for voters.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: We will learn from the experiences of other countries that are holding elections even during this on-going COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: All these measures and precautions are required to protect Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is a very important question and it is an issue that we are addressing and that we are paying a lot of attention to.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For the enforcement of the Stay-Home Notice, we have help from the Home Team, so may I ask the Minister for Home Affairs, Mr K Shanmugam to respond.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Singapore residents and long-term pass holders, they will obviously come back and they will be placed under a Stay-Home Notice (SHN) from 23 March.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And it works this way: it means that Singaporeans will not be stranded overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They can get access to our healthcare system.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But those who are served with an SHN also have a responsibility.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They should not put the wider community at risk.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: A Stay-Home Notice means exactly that – they have to remain in their place of residence at all times during the 14-day period and that is a non-negotiable condition.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Persons on SHN are required to monitor their health closely.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They have to minimise contact with others, even at home.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They cannot leave the house and they have to seek immediate medical attention if feeling unwell.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This is because persons under SHN carry some risk of having the virus by virtue of their travel history or by virtue of their contact with others who may have had COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: To ensure compliance with SHN, we conduct enforcement checks.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They include surveillance using SMS, web-based solutions, mobile applications; and people are expected to be at home and contactable, obviously.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Those who do not respond to the messages will be called and there are also house visits, unannounced, by enforcement officers.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: You have section 21(a) of the Infectious Diseases Act (IDA).

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: MOH will be setting out new regulations under the IDA, specifically focusing on penalties for SHN breaches.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The jail term could be up to six months, a $10,000 fine, or both.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, the passes could be cancelled if you are short-term visitors and you could be asked to leave Singapore immediately and barred from re-entry forever.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Foreign employees could have their work passes revoked and repatriated.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For students, action can be taken by schools, including suspension or dismissal.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Where there has a breach of the SHN and we knew about it, action had been taken.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Members may recall when the SHNs were first introduced.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There was a 45-year-old Permanent Resident, he was served with such a notice.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He had a travel history to mainland China at that point, failed to respond to our calls.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: When enforcement checks were done, he was not at home and then, he was seen at Changi Airport, wanting to leave Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is clearly a breach of his SHN.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, his application for renewal of his re-entry permit was rejected by ICA and his PR status therefore was effectively revoked, and he has been barred from coming into Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: NIE terminated a foreign student from his postgraduate course, again for breaching his SHN and for repeatedly providing false information to NIE regarding his travel movements.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I think Er Dr Lee's question may have been prompted by some of the messages that many of us have seen going around about recent returnees, particularly from the United Kingdom, that they are going out to eat local food, they hold birthday parties in their homes, they interact with friends, they go to clubs, bars and so on, while they were under SHNs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And many Singaporeans get upset when they hear about this.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I think, either today or yesterday, another case was reported on an online site, Mothership – a Singaporean returning from Myanmar was apparently issued a SHN but he went out to have "bak kut teh" and posted about it on his Facebook page.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I have asked for that case to be investigated.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are trying to verify some of these messages on SHNs being flouted.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If anyone, a member of public, if you have information about such behaviour, please give it to the Police.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will follow up and we cannot allow such behaviour.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, I have given very clear instructions where these cases are verified to be true, we will charge them in Court.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The second point is, when people are required to declare their travel history, there has to be honesty.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Where false information is given, in order to avoid SHNs, there can be prosecution.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Section 182 of the Penal Code carries a jail term of up two years or fine.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Section 57(1)(g) of the Immigration Act also carries a jail term of up to 12 months, up to $4,000 fine, or both.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But there is a wider duty that each of us owes to control the spread of COVID-19 and, really, not to endanger others and expose them to infection.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: One story going around – again, we are trying to verify – is that an individual is said to have gone for a holiday in Italy, developed symptoms of COVID-19 with a cough, fever and breathlessness.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And this person apparently hid his symptoms and travel history in order to get on to a plane to come back to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And later, in Singapore, the person was admitted to the hospital, fell very ill, found to be carrying the virus.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If this is true, the conduct is highly irresponsible.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I can understand, as a Singaporean, he is anxious to come home, to his family.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He is confident about our healthcare system, he wants to be here, but not at the risk of endangering other people's well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He should have declared his symptoms at check-in.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Then, the airline would make a considered decision whether to allow the person to fly, and if so, with what sort of precautions.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There cannot be this sort of unacceptable risk of infecting others.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have also received feedback from healthcare workers that some people are not truthful with their travel history when they see their GPs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Our healthcare professionals, as Mr Gan has said, are our key asset in this fight.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That information would allow us to identify persons who may be at risk, take precautions and provide them with the appropriate medical care.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But regulations and strong enforcement are not going to be enough on their own, if people continue to insist on being irresponsible.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: All Singaporeans have to do our part, exercise social responsibility, protect ourselves, friends and family and fellow citizens.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The public officials – you have heard Minister Lawrence – have been working around the clock.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And it has really been quite an exhausting few months for them.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Most Singaporeans – you see it from the reaction – a vast majority of Singaporeans are responsible, understand this and have come together and acted admirably.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: When we come together as a people, looking out for one another, we will prevail and we will overcome this COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The two Ministers, the co-chairs the Multi-Ministry Task Force, thanked many people.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But I think we should also thank the members of the Multi-Ministry Task Force for their leadership in the last two months in guiding us through this crisis.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The first is, under what circumstances will we consider a complete lockdown of the country.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many people have mentioned this and referred to other jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But what are the implications to our country if we should adopt this measure.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I know of many who are attempting to come back to Singapore, but with increasing lockdowns and travel restrictions, what assistance are we providing to Singaporeans overseas who are attempting to come back to Singapore?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The last question is in relation to the fact that Singapore is a pluralistic society, we are multi-religious and there are four major religious festivals coming up.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have Qingming Festival, Clear Bright Festival, Good Friday Easter, Ramadan as well as Vesak Day coming up on our calendars in the next two months.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What are the advice and guidelines that religious institutions as well as believers should follow as we come close to these festivals in terms of gathering together and celebrating?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But let us look specifically at what additional measures we are contemplating, and I mentioned that just now.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have already put in place quite strict measures recently.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They go together because if you were to suspend schools, many parents will need help looking after their children.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And if they have to go to work, it will not be practical.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will be very difficult for them to do.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, the next step if we have to consider, what would be the considerations for that?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not just the overall number of cases.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have to drill deeper to understand the reasons for these cases.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the many Singaporeans who need assistance, we remain open to welcoming them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, I think that if there is a need to, MFA and the overseas missions are reaching out to them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Flights have come down but commercial flights are still available for many of these countries.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, I would imagine people are making their own arrangements.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some have decided to stay and then some will decide to come back.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And when they come back, we welcome them but we take the necessary precautions to make sure that they self isolate for the full period and do not cause any infection within our own community.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The religious places of worships may remain open for people to go; individuals who need to get help from their religious leaders, that remains.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Religious organisations, different faiths may want to do smaller groups.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But if they do so, then we ask them to abide strictly by the guidelines.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Each group less than 10 persons; and even within that grouping, make sure precautions are taken.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, minimise physical contact as much as possible and then, make sure that no one there is unwell.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If anyone has been overseas recently, make sure that they are isolated.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They should not be there to begin with.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, these are all precautions that religious organisations, in fact, every organisation should take.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If there is a small group, keep it less than 10 and even then, take all the necessary precautions.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: First, I would like to declare my interest as a director of two SGX-listed companies.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My work also requires me to advise SGX-listed companies.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, with the latest measures, will there be legislative amendments to allow such corporate actions to be passed during this period?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have two clarifications for the Minister for Health.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, it is concerning the lethality of the virus.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Earlier, he mentioned that if persons are young and healthy, even if they catch the virus, they are likely to get away with mild symptoms, such as a cough.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And to get a sense of perspective, there have been some leaders overseas who have given a rough figure to say that 95% of the population need not worry about serious complications from COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister whether he agrees that based on the experience we have had in Singapore, that this 95% to 5% proportion is also what we have seen in Singapore, meaning that only 5% who encounter the virus are likely to have serious complications.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second clarification is, could he give some information on the profile of the ICU patients with COVID-19?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We know so far that the two deaths have concerned those who are elderly and with pre-existing conditions, but are there also significant numbers of patients in the ICU who are younger and do not have pre-existing conditions?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It does not mean that the young do not have to take the disease seriously.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
