text: Because there is always a risk that if you have more people, even young people, getting COVID-19, you may pass it on to the old people around you, including those with chronic diseases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is true from our data that those older patients and those with underlying chronic diseases, like cardiovascular diseases, tend to have more serious disease outcomes.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is important for us to enhance our protection for the elderly but we must not take the disease lightly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: From our own experience in the ICU in our hospitals, we do see some young people who develop serious diseases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Part of the reason – I think I have explained during the last Sitting – is because of their auto immune system overreacting to the disease and therefore, it causes damage to their organs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We do have one or two patients in our ICU who are young and who happen to have very serious disease outcomes.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But it is, I think, generally correct to say that this disease is likely to affect the seniors more severely and especially those with underlying chronic conditions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we have to pay particular attention to the seniors among us, but as the Prime Minister commented just now, even if young people get it, there is a risk that you pass it on to your family members, including the seniors in your family.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: MOH has issued a set of guidelines for seniors as well as for young people when you interact with seniors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Do not just leave it to the seniors to protect themselves and we happily go to their homes to say "Hello" to them and share a dinner with them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We may be the vector, we may be the cause of their infection.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, do take precautions if you want to visit your seniors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think it is not possible to ask ourselves to stop visiting seniors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have to continue to visit them, but when you do so, exercise caution and practise a high level of personal hygiene, particularly when you are dealing with seniors.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, I was very happy to hear of this new move to decant some of the less serious cases to community facilities.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would just like to ask whether considerations have been made to do what some other countries have done and allow the milder cases to self-isolate.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Because if we do see larger numbers, that may even exceed the capacity of these community facilities.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The second is that I was also very happy to hear the very high level of testing in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Because there have been some comments over the past weeks that perhaps Singapore has not been testing as much as other countries.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I was very happy to hear of the very high level of testing that we have had.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The clarification concerns whether we should consider testing those who have completed their QOs or the SHNs.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Because there have been some concerns raised by certain experts that these people have been quarantined, could actually have developed very mild forms during that period – the 14 days.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So far, we have a relatively high level of testing.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Because testing is not only laborious, it also requires resources to be put in place; not just for the testing but for the laboratory resources as well.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is very important for us to ensure that we are very targeted and focus on those who are at higher risk of infection.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, for those who are under the Quarantine Orders or SHN, we also do risk assessment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, you should be always careful and mindful.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Even for those who have been discharged, you must continue to be careful because if you are not infected, after you have left the quarantine facility, you may get infected.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It does not ensure that you have lifelong immunity because you have never been infected before.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We must assume that everyone has a potential of being infected, so we take the necessary precautions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This pertains to the new and heightened restrictions announced yesterday evening by Minister, which were also the subject of his speech today.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Since the release of the Electoral Boundary Review Committee report, I think it is quite apparent to a lot of Singaporeans that political parties have stepped up their political outreach.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The concern in view of yesterday's announcements is that some of this these outreach activities can easily lead to the formation of large social gatherings in excess of 10 individuals, in close proximity to each other.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Does the Minister not agree that such continued outreach could potentially interfere and contradict the directives of the task force, particularly yesterday's new directives?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Because to quote the Minister, there was a concern that the safe distancing measures were not being taken seriously and that the public was generally too slow to respond to the new COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Two for the Minister for Health, two for Minister for National Development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: For Minister for Health, are there any plans by the Government to provide housing support to frontline healthcare workers who request it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: That is because we have heard that there are some cases of healthcare workers, who out of caution, they want to isolate themselves from their families and they may or may not have the means to do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The second question is there are some reports elsewhere that indicate quite a high proportion of cases actually have no symptoms.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: For example, I think about half of the cases from The Diamond Princess cruise ship were non-symptomatic upon being diagnosed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, are there any plans to investigate this in Singapore, for example, through voluntary random testing or something, to see whether we do in fact have quite a few people who were exposed and infected but there is nothing, no consequences there?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Because this could help to inform our strategy going forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: For Minister for National Development, in the event of more strict control measures, what resources will be deployed to ensure that daily necessities can be distributed to the public, especially for those who are more vulnerable and in need because they may not be able to leave their home or may be very cautious about doing so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We do not want a situation where people cannot access daily necessities in the event of more strict measures.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The other question on more strict measures is, currently, what are we doing to define essential services and to work with workplaces, employers and so on, so that everybody understands what is essential and what is not.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Because I think we are seeing in many other countries, there is a lot of confusion about how this is being worked out on the ground.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: And I think if we have more strict measures and we rush to inform everybody, you are essential and you are not, we will have a lot of confusion and that could be too late.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If they have this requirement, please let us know and we will try our best to help some of our frontline workers are staying in rented houses or rented apartments – we do want to appeal to the landlords to allow them to continue to stay in these apartments.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In the hospital, they are given protective gear so they are safe, so allow them to continue.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But for healthcare workers who do need housing support, we have been working with the Clusters' management to extend our support to them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That means people who are infected that do not have symptoms or they have mild symptoms or their symptoms are so mild that patient themselves do not know that they have such an infection.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But it is also professionally assessed that for those with very mild symptoms or no symptoms at all, they are unlikely to spread because the spreading requires the projection of your droplets and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Studies have shown that for the mild symptom cases, the risk of transmission is significantly lower.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, some of these experiments and surveys are on-going.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Even under today's environment where we put in place the range of measures that we have already announced, we were mindful of that and that is why we are still allowing F&B outlets to operate, people still need to go out to eat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Second, on the question on the framework for essential services, we do have such a framework in place and we will engage the key stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Of course, when the announcements – if and when announcements are made for stricter measures including closure of workplaces, aside from those doing essential services, then that would be announced.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think the Member's point is by the time you announce and put out the framework, people may well be scrambling and the reaction time may not be fast enough and there may be a little bit of anxiety at that point in time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will do what we can and we are doing what we can to engage these firms.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think the firms who are tagged as essential services know who they are.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The ones that do not, probably do not quite know and may think that they are essential even though they are not part of the framework.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we will be reaching out to more firms so that they are mindful and if additional measures are needed, we can ensure a smoother transition.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I deeply appreciate all the efforts that have been put in so far.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: It is so good to be a Singaporean.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Given the call for heightened vigilance and enhanced measures for various reasons amongst which is also to reduce the risk of infection to innocent others around us, I would like to ask what would be done to enforce or curb behaviours that may pose risks to the public health of others and whether our laws and our current tools are sufficient to do so?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In my constituency, there is one man who has been very recalcitrant.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: What he did was that he lined his fingers with his saliva and just touched all the lift buttons.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: There would be saliva left behind on the panel.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: And so, currently, it is being looked into.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: However, there is concern to the public health of other residents who have to share the lift.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, I would like to ask whether we are adequately equipped to take action on such a very inconsiderate individual.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Member can give us the details and we will follow up on this particular case.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think the Minister for Home Affairs has already talked about those who fail to comply with our Stay-Home Notices and Quarantine Orders.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I will encourage members of the public – if you come across any of these actions that put public safety or health in danger, do let us know and we will go after them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We need everyone to play their part to keep Singapore safe and healthy.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The first one is: what are we doing with the safe distancing measures in public transport?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I am a public commuter so I have not seen any changes in that regard.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The third point is relating to the communications on the advisories that are going out.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: It is very rapid, it is also changing as what Minister Wong says, every other day.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Some of the elderly folks have shared with me they are not able to keep up with what is going on.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I am just wondering if there could be — well, first, I would like to understand how we are actually getting the information out to the different segments of the society; and secondly, if there is a central agency that is managing this in the form of FAQs or handling queries from citizens when they are not sure about is nine persons in terms of gatherings okay; and if a gathering is for community work instead of social gathering, is that okay?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: There are a lot of questions that are coming out and I wonder if there is a need for a central agency to handle that.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I will leave it to Minister Wong to talk about public transport as well as the advisory.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I should also take this opportunity to thank Minister for Communications and Information, Mr Iswaran, who is always in the background.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But his Ministry and him have been very crucial; they play a very vital role in managing our public communications, the WhatsApp that you receive from Gov.sg came from the Ministry, so we want to thank MCI for their hard work.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We always try to have a benchmark beyond which we turn on the switch or turn off the switch.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But in the healthcare system, we do not operate like that.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We look at the whole scenario and disease pattern, and we adjust as we go along.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, even today, if you ask me, we are under pressure too.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Our resources are stretched but we make adjustments to accommodate the trend of the growing number of cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If the cases continue to grow we will continue to adjust.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These are our strategies to keep our healthcare system moving and still maintaining certain buffer capacity, in case there is a surge.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Unfortunately, I would not be able to give you a single number because it is really a whole set of conditions and we adjust as we go along.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think we have sufficient flexibility in the healthcare system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have issued the advisories; the Public Sector is going all out to do it.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But, as I mentioned earlier, we know that more still can be done and has to be done.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On communications, as Minister Gan said, we have a whole-of-Government approach.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: MOH is the front because you see the statements, advisories, they are all put out under the banner of MOH.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All of the information is on the MOH website, but really behind the scenes is a whole-of-Government communications team coordinated by Minister Iswaran and the MCI communications team.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: A lot of people are working day and night because of the rapid – the nature of the work is such that we are putting out new information so rapidly, so they are constantly generating infographics, materials in different languages and pushing them pushing them out through multiple platforms.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think the team will always look at ways in which it can do better, particularly reaching out to segments that may not be accessing the information so readily and we will always look at different ways where we can put up more information.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We know it is a vital work that has to be done and we are sparing no effort to ensure that the information is put out in a timely and accurate manner.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also, during this period, be able to leverage on resources outside of the Public Sector.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, there is spare capacity out in the private sector.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are call centres, there are people who can be enlisted to help us in this outreach and so we are also looking at leveraging on these resources, so it need not and should not be a Government effort alone.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We really need a whole of Singapore effort in order to fight the virus.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I want to thank the Ministers for their statements, especially Minister Lawrence Wong earlier for the reassurance that Singaporeans who are returning to Singapore after spending some time overseas, will be able to come back to the haven that we all call home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to see if other measures are needed.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I am just very mindful that for every new measure we put in place, there is a requirement to have new operational requirements, new processes, new staff work to be done and all of this takes up resources.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, at the end of the day, this is about looking at how we allocate resources to areas of urgent needs and priorities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will first monitor the volume of outflows.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is already coming down and if the measures we have are effective in bringing the volumes down further, I think we should be all right.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In any case, I think there will still be some people who might very well need to travel, for whatever reasons – maybe there is a bereavement, that somebody had passed away in the family, outside of Singapore and they really need to go and I can understand why.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, I do not think the numbers will fall to zero but if it comes down to a number that we are able to manage, we should be okay.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But if the numbers continue to persist and do not come down further, then, indeed more measures will be necessary and we will consider what additional measures at that stage will be introduced.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The contact tracing is also done by our Police officers from Singapore Police Force.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Just wanted to seek clarification on whether their policing work is impacted by the amount of the time they are spending with the contact tracing?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: So, how much of this is impacting the Police work?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The question is on misinformation with regards to things like live telecast of Prime Minister's speech that was circulated on WhatsApp, call for volunteers at MOH call centres, impending lockdown and so on.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: A lot of the misinformation is sent on private messaging platforms and timely clarifications are posted on MOH website and various other websites.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Is it worthwhile considering setting up just a microsite just for all these clarifications to be posted so that people can have a one-stop place where we can see what is being circulated and timely responses are posted and we can always refer to it as a first touch point.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: And third on social distancing on public transport, I hear Minister Lawrence Wong's comments.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I think it is very important to encourage telecommuting amongst our workforce to reduce the travellers commuting at peak times and so on.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: But the point is, if you go to public transport sites – bus stations, MRT stations and so on – even at the escalators, people are just lining up back to back of each other.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: That is not just during peak hours but also non-peak hours.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: So, how can we implement safe distancing within bus stations, within MRT stations and also on the bus itself we can have one seat beside each other to be vacant, we can actually Implement some sort of measures even on the MRT trains to have one seat in between each other.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: So, I think more thought can be given on that because if you are encouraging safe distancing everywhere and we have public transportation where a lot of people are moving in masses —

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: It is an area we can look at.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: We have a policy of people coming back from overseas to be issued Stay-Home Notice but however, Singaporeans who want to visit their relatives who just came back and visit the houses, how can we discourage them from doing so?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Because there have been cases where they go and visit the people who are staying at home, even though they limit the exposure time but it is still exposure.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I will answer on behalf of Minister for Home Affairs on Police work.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: First, I want to thank the Police for helping us to do contact tracing.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On the misinformation, I will ask Minister Iswaran to respond in a while.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I will ask Minister Wong to answer the rest of the questions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will address the question on public transport.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Irshad is right that we should have safe distancing measures even within the public transport system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But the first priority has to be just to reduce the numbers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If the numbers are still high, having safe distancing within a train or bus will mean the queue goes up somewhere else.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The only way to do that, as I said earlier – telecommuting, staggered hours, all employers must push harder on this.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, for a start, the Multi-Ministry Task Force co-chairs together with, usually the Director for Medical Services as well as other Ministers as appropriate and other officials as appropriate, have been conducting regular press conferences.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And this has been an important part of our effort to ensure that there is regular communication and also regular representation – faces associated with the communications – so that Singaporeans have a point of focus and a point of assurance in this entire effort.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This occurs as I have said, in the background, but it is a very important part of ensuring that the media understand the context of the decisions that are being made and the rationale, so that, when they report and convey those decisions, they can contextualise these correctly.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Thirdly, the Member has raised specifically the point on misinformation, we have had to deal with it through a variety of measures.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Of course, in the most extreme circumstances, we have had to use some of the powers available to us under the newly enacted POFMA legislation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think Members will be aware of that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have also tried to use other channels to push out information proactively but also sometimes reactively.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, in some of the instances that the Member has cited, for example, when there was a information passing around about Prime Minister's impending address to the nation and all kinds of rumours associated with it, we did push out something through the gov.sg WhatsApp.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The last point I want to make in response to the Member's comment that, whilst we can consider things like microsites and so on, as a kind of inventory of some of these clarifications that we put out, the crux of the matter really is in being able to counter such misinformation quickly.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I think we can do that in two ways.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The first is, of course, on the part of the Government in terms of how we are able to put out the information, the correct information through all the channels available to us and we will continue to work at it and improve on it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The second is – I think this is largely the most important point – what Singaporeans can do ourselves and I think it has been salutary to see how Singaporeans now – often I get a lot of these messages and I am sure Members do too – the first instinct is ask: is this correct or is this fake?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I think that instinct is the right one, not to immediately press forward and pass it on to all our chat groups.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But, to first verify, understand, before we share.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think if we do that, that will be the strongest defence against misinformation.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Am I correct to say that already half of NCID's ICUs are taken up?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: What will happen when it reaches its full capacity?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: And may I also ask the Minister, so far, what is the average length of stay of patients in our ICU beds by COVID-19 cases?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Because we do want to make sure that our healthcare manpower are properly deployed in the most impactful place.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Many of them are very stretched and very tired, and some of them have fatigue.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We try to support them as much as we can, but what is most important is all of us do our part to keep the numbers low, to keep the cases low, to help prevent transmission.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In this way, we will do our part in helping these healthcare workers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We do have flexibility to expand our ICU capacity, if necessary.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In terms of average length of stay, it is very difficult to have average length of stay for ICU because each case is quite different.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There are some cases who went in for a few days, they are able to recover.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is not very meaningful to have average length of stay in terms of ICU because it does differ from patient to patient.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Generally, for those who go into ICU, they tend to stay a bit longer because the conditions are more serious.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We do keep a lookout for them, we try to provide them with as much support as possible, because in the end, for infections like COVID-19, we depend to a large extent, on their own immunity system to take over, to fight the infection.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Could I ask the Minister to shed some clarity on the rationale behind the action to be taken in the event that a there is an infected staff or pupil in a school.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, what is the rationale behind decisions, for example, in deciding whether a school should be closed for the day for cleaning or should be close for two weeks or whether Stay-Home Notices should be issued to pupils and staff.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think some parents would like to know more details of this.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My second question relating to our manpower needs.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe I have asked a Parliamentary Question relating to this.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How many of them have returned and if they have not returned, when are they expected to return?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And this is done through the MOH team – they go down, they assess, they make a very thorough investigation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, there is an objective and very thorough assessment made in each and every case.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A good number of them have not returned.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Actually, that number that is flowing through every day has been slowed to a trickle.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Whereas, for foreign work pass holders, we have asked them to stay out of Singapore for the time being and then, when the situation enables us to facilitate their return, we will do so.
